title: rate limits made the bot think an order was still open
author: Plane-Increase-2122
selftext:
last night i noticed one of my market-making workers had stopped placing new orders even though the process was healthy. there were no crashes and the heartbeat looked normal. the problem was that the worker had hit the exchange request limit while cancelling stale quotes, then interpreted several failed balance and order queries as temporary empty responses. that created a bad state in the local database. the bot believed two orders were open, so it kept trying to cancel them on every loop. the cancel requests were mostly rejected because the orders had already filled, but the fill updates were delayed behind the same rate-limited request queue. meanwhile the strategy was holding less quote currency than the risk check expected. i found it by comparing the exchange trade history with the worker logs and then replaying the last few account events in a test process. the fix wasn't changing the signal logic. i separated private account requests from public market-data calls, added jitter to the retry delay, and made a filled or already-cancelled response trigger a fresh execution lookup instead of another blind cancel. as a second check, i looked at the relevant public addresses through a block explorer and cryptowallet-balance. both showed the expected assets on chain, although neither can explain the exchange's internal available balance. that helped narrow it down to reconciliation and API handling rather than a withdrawal or settlement problem

i'm now recording request headers, response status, and the last acknowledged event id for each worker. the bot recovered after a manual restart, but i don't want restarts to be part of the normal recovery path. the annoying part is that the trading strategy was fine; the bookkeeping around ordinary rate-limit errors was not

comments.author: Trick-Refrigerator37
comments.body: We hit a similar loop on Kraken after treating a timeout as an empty open-orders result. The dangerous part was not the failed cancel itself, but committing that assumption before the next user-trades page had arrived. We now keep an order in an unknown state after any 429 or transport failure, block replacement quoting for that symbol, and reconcile from executions first. Did you add a maximum age for unknown orders, or does your worker wait indefinitely for an acknowledged event
